key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term perovskite photoluminescence degradation from early time-series data, even for unseen samples.
engineering_relevance: This could substantially shorten stability testing workflows for new perovskite formulations by reducing the need for long accelerated-aging experiments.
method: Collected 86k+ photoluminescence spectra from 167 metal halide perovskites under heat and light stress
Featurized spectra with a physics-informed model to capture degradation-relevant descriptors
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity and generalize across material groups
evidence_signal: The abstract reports diverse data from 167 perovskites and states the model outperforms baseline benchmarks on unseen samples.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and representativeness of the stressed training data, so transfer to new chemistries or lighting/temperature conditions should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
